headline: EVOLUTION MINING TAKES 9.9% OF ARIZONA GOLD & SILVER — C$12M CLOSED, OATMAN DRILL DRIVE FUNDED THROUGH 2027
snippet: Arizona Gold & Silver Inc. (TSXV: AZS; OTCQB: AZASF) closed its C$12 million strategic investment from Evolution Mining Gold Operations Ltd. — a wholly owned subsidiary of ASX-listed producer Evolution Mining — on August 20. Evolution acquired 15,056,004 units at C$0.80 per unit, giving the Australian mid-tier producer roughly 9.9% of AZS on a partially diluted basis. Each unit pairs one common share with half a warrant exercisable at C$1.00 for three years. Arizona will spend at least 90% of proceeds — approximately C$10.8 million — accelerating exploration at its Philadelphia Gold-Silver Project in Arizona's Oatman Mining District. A permitted, funded, and now major-backed U.S. gold-silver explorer at 9.9% is exactly the strategic template late-cycle producers are running to secure the next generation of pipeline ounces.

headline: IRRUPTIVE (IRR) DRILLS 795.2M AT 0.66% CuEq AT PIMENTÓN — 60M CORE AT 1.49% CuEq CONFIRMS CENTRAL CHILEAN PORPHYRY
snippet: Irruptive Metals Corp. (TSXV: IRR) reported August 20 assay results from its first 3,084-metre diamond drill campaign across four holes at the Pimentón Cu-Au porphyry project in Chile's V Region. Hole IMP002 returned 795.2 metres grading 0.66% CuEq (0.41 g/t Au, 0.31% Cu) from 167 m to end of hole at 962.2 m — including a 60-metre gold-dominant high-grade interval at 1.49% CuEq (1.37 g/t Au, 0.31% Cu). Hole IMP004 returned 406 metres at 0.47% CuEq. The results confirm and extend historical drilling completed by Rio Tinto and Anglo American, demonstrating geological continuity across the Central target area. A near-kilometre downhole intercept above 0.6% CuEq puts Pimentón into the size range that attracts strategic Chilean copper interest — precisely when LME copper is trading within striking distance of all-time highs on structurally tight forward supply.

headline: CADILLAC MINES DRILLS 2.13 g/t Au OVER 38.2M AT KERR-ADDISON — LASSONDE-BACKED INFILL CONVERTS WASTE TO ORE FOR 2026 MRE
snippet: Cadillac Mines released August 19 significant high-grade infill drill results from within the Kerr-Addison open pit at Virginiatown, Ontario — highlighted by hole KAD26-397 returning 2.13 g/t gold over 38.2 metres from 192 metres downhole. The results comprise the first 29 infill diamond drill holes totalling 11,569 metres of a planned 17,850-metre program designed to upgrade the 2026 Mineral Resource Estimate. Management stressed the infill program's dual purpose: converting previously modelled waste rock inside the pit shell to economic mineralization, and lifting the confidence category on existing inferred and indicated ounces. Cadillac is backed by Pierre Lassonde's family office — a signal-quality endorsement in the historic Kirkland Lake-Virginiatown gold camp as the sector rotates back into resource-conversion stories at $4,500 gold.

headline: NEXGOLD HITS 5.26 g/t Au OVER 7M + 7.08 g/t Au OVER 5M AT GOLDBORO — 76% OF NOVA SCOTIA RC INFILL DONE AHEAD OF BUILD DECISION
snippet: NexGold Mining Corp. (TSXV: NEXG) announced August 19 additional results from the RC infill drill program at the Goldboro Gold Project in Nova Scotia: 5.26 g/t gold over 7.0 metres and 7.08 g/t gold over 5.0 metres. The RC program targets the west and east pits at 12.5-metre nominal spacing to 50-metre depth and is now over 76% complete, feeding directly into the imminent construction decision for the fully permitted Goldboro build. With the Q2 update highlighting build readiness and this RC batch demonstrating grade continuity through the near-surface pit envelope, the stack of catalysts — construction decision, financing, groundbreaking — is compressing toward a September–October window as gold trades above $4,480.

headline: DUNDEE + WESTHAVEN: 5TH SHOVELNOSE INFILL BATCH "MOST ENCOURAGING TO DATE" — HIGH-GRADE AT DEPTH AND ON MARGIN OF SOUTH ZONE
snippet: Dundee Corporation released August 20 the fifth batch of assay results from the ongoing 35,000-metre resource infill drilling program at Westhaven Gold Corp's (TSXV: WHN) South Zone gold-silver deposit on the Shovelnose property in southern British Columbia's Spences Bridge Gold Belt. Dundee's CEO described the results — including high-grade intercepts at depth and along the southeastern margin of the deposit — as "exceptional... among the most encouraging we have seen from the program to date." Dundee is earning up to 60% in Westhaven's four Spences Bridge properties through up to C$85 million in staged expenditures, with a minimum C$30 million commitment inclusive of a fully funded 50,000-metre drill program. Extension mineralization at depth beyond the current resource envelope is the type of result that drives the eventual PEA/PFS toward larger tonnage — the exact scenario Dundee's earn-in is designed to bankroll.

headline: LABRADOR GOLD INVESTS US$1.41M IN SAN CRISTOBAL — BOLIVIA'S FLAGSHIP SILVER-ZINC-LEAD MINE JOINS THE PORTFOLIO
snippet: Labrador Gold Corp. (TSXV: LAB) announced August 20 the closing of a US$1,410,000 investment in privately-held San Cristobal Mining Inc., which owns 100% of Minera San Cristóbal S.A. — operator of the San Cristóbal silver-zinc-lead mine in Bolivia, one of the largest primary silver-zinc mines in the world. San Cristóbal produced approximately 12 million ounces of silver and 235,000 tonnes of zinc-in-concentrate in a typical year of full operation. The transaction gives Labrador Gold minority exposure to a producing polymetallic asset while retaining its exploration focus, and marks a rare cross-border strategic pivot for a Canadian junior — an interesting signal on both the silver bull case and the accessibility of Bolivian mining assets under the current government.

headline: GOLD PULLS BACK TO $4,481, SILVER HOLDS $68.90 — 24-HOUR DIGESTION AFTER 4.13% TREASURY-BUYBACK SURGE, WARSH KEYNOTE 8 DAYS OUT
snippet: Spot gold traded at approximately $4,481.29 per ounce at 1:55 PM EDT on Thursday August 20 — down 0.81% on the session — as traders digested Wednesday's 4.13% Treasury-buyback rally that had pushed the metal to $4,512. Silver traded at $68.90/oz, effectively holding the +6.39% Wednesday gain to $66.97 and extending into a fresh multi-week high. Gold is still up more than 10% for August; September rate-hike odds remain suppressed at ~33%. The tape structure — a modest first-day fade after an outsized-volume advance — is textbook consolidation rather than reversal, and with Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote just eight sessions out on August 28, positioning risk is now the dominant near-term driver.

headline: GDX/GDXJ UP 21-22% IN FIVE DAYS, $419M RETAIL AUGUST INFLOWS — MINERS FINALLY CATCHING UP TO GOLD'S NEW HIGHS
snippet: Gold mining ETFs broke decisively higher this week, with the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) rising 21.09% over five days to $89.73 and the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ) rising 22.42% to $116.78 — trading intraday to $126.55 on August 20 within a 52-week range of $72.91-$157.49. The move breaks the miners out of a months-long falling wedge and comes as GDX's August retail inflows hit $419 million, the strongest monthly intake since February. The GoldSeek Q2'26 fundamentals piece separately established that miner sector cash treasuries hit $41.3 billion (record), Q2 operating cash flow reached $17.2 billion, and AISC margins averaged $2,914/oz — with the sector trailing P/E compressed to 16.5x (lowest in 41 quarters). Record cash, record margins, lowest relative valuation in a decade, and now finally the retail bid: the late-cycle re-rating setup has begun to fire.

headline: MONEY METALS: "THE DEBT BLACK HOLE" — WHY PRIVATE CREDIT DISTORTION IS THE MONETARY BACKDROP FOR THE GOLD BULL
snippet: Money Metals Exchange published August 19 an opinion piece titled "How the Debt Black Hole Is Warping the Economy: Private Credit Markets," arguing that the explosive growth of the private credit and shadow banking system — now a multi-trillion-dollar parallel to regulated banking — is quietly distorting the mechanisms through which Federal Reserve policy transmits into the real economy. For gold and silver holders, the piece frames the metal bid not as a rate-cut trade but as a hedge against a monetary architecture in which the Fed can no longer fully see, let alone control, the credit expansion happening off its balance sheet. This is the structural counterpart to the flow story (record central bank buying, GDX inflows): the reason the physical demand keeps coming back regardless of near-term rate paths.

headline: COMEX SILVER: SEPT FIRST NOTICE 7 DAYS OUT — 264.2M oz STILL OPEN AGAINST 99.5M oz REGISTERED, 6.1× PAPER LEVERAGE
snippet: COMEX silver vaults hold 337.3 million troy ounces total as of August 19 — 99.5 million registered (deliverable against futures) and 237.8 million eligible — up from 76 million registered in March. September first notice day is seven business days away with 52,838 contracts (264.2 million ounces) still open, giving a coverage ratio of 16.5% and paper leverage of 6.1×. Delivery volume has remained elevated through August but registered stocks have not been drained, suggesting real physical is flowing to satisfy contracts without triggering a hard squeeze — yet. For silver miners and holders, the September delivery cycle is the operational counterpart to the sentiment story: if a single large stopper opts for delivery instead of rolling, the coverage ratio compresses fast at these leverage levels.
